teaser.en: Bite a leaf and you taste the sea: this succulent shrub is so salty that only hardy livestock will browse it.

summary.en: Seablite is a salty, succulent shrub of the landward mangrove edge and the bare saline flats behind it. Where it grows it often takes over, forming low grey-green thickets where little else survives.

about.en:
Seablite is a low, much-branched shrub with small, fleshy, almost cylindrical leaves packed along its stems. The leaves store water and salt, which lets the plant survive on ground that would kill most others. Its flowers are tiny and greenish and easy to overlook.

Where conditions suit it, seablite is often the dominant plant, covering patches of the flats in a single dense stand.

where.en: It grows on the landward side of the mangroves and on saline flats, the open, salt-crusted ground that the highest tides flood only now and then. Walk inland from the mangroves at Gazi or Vanga and it is one of the plants that marks the change from mud to dry land.

uses.en: It is used as fodder, though it is very salty. Inland, pastoralists use it to feed their animals.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. In Swahili it is *mwinyonye*, and it is also called *mwinamia maji*. In English it is seablite, and its scientific name is *Suaeda monoica*.

reason.en: The grey mangrove also thrives in very salty ground
Another salt-hardy shrub, with a similar name
Grows at the same landward high-water edge
